Current safety benchmarks focus on harmful content, not behavioral alignment during instrumental goal conflicts. To address this, we introduce PacifAIst, a benchmark of 700 scenarios testing self-preservation, resource acquisition, and deception. We evaluated eight state-of-the-art large language models, revealing a significant performance hierarchy. Google’s Gemini 2.5 Flash demonstrated the strongest human-centric alignment (90.31%), while the highly anticipated GPT-5 scored lowest (79.49%), indicating potential risks. These findings establish an urgent need to shift the focus of AI safety evaluation from what models say to what they would do, ensuring that autonomous systems are not just helpful in theory but are provably safe in practice.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.3390/ai6100256\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 10, 2]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7554/elife.77285.sa0\", \"title\": [\"Editor's evaluation: Transcriptome-wide association study and eQTL colocalization identify potentially causal genes responsible for human bone mineral density GWAS associations\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7554/elife.77285.sa0\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 4, 25]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "54d53fa507129c8fa583e9dc58d8d01980bdf4fe…
